category_title: Student with language impairment who shouts out and disrupts others to avoid difficult tasks
scenario_title: Independent worksheet completion during pull-out special education work time
minimal_context: James is sitting at his desk in the pull-out special education classroom working on an independent reading worksheet while other students work nearby.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Here is your independent reading worksheet, James. Please complete these questions quietly at your desk.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Pushes the worksheet away) I'm not doing this. It's too hard.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just try your best and see what you can do.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Starts tapping his pencil loudly on the desk and looks away from the paper) I said I'm not doing it!

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please keep your voice down and focus on your own paper.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Stands up and shouts across the room) HEY! Look at me! This reading is stupid! (Reaches over and grabs the worksheet off the desk of the student sitting next to him)

task.content: Independent reading, math, or writing worksheets that the student, with assistance, was unlikely to complete with 50% or better accuracy

context.environment: General classroom instruction and work time in a pull-out special education classroom at an elementary school
context.materials: Independent reading, math, or writing worksheets

challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Repeated failure experienced across their schooling
